## What I changed

**`src/files/entities.rs`** — `EntityFile::from_content` now rejects a `status: pruned` file that still carries a non-empty title or body (whitespace-trimmed), returning `FrontmatterError::Parse`. Legitimate tombstones (empty title + body, exactly what `run_prune` writes) still parse and sync. [entities.rs:244-253](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_ed78398f_l6be7hp0/src/files/entities.rs)

**`src/storage/events.rs`** — new `scrub_entity_payloads(conn, entity_ids)`: batched, chunked `UPDATE events SET payload = json_remove(payload, '$.old_content', '$.new_content', '$.title')`. Event rows, types, and timestamps are preserved; only content-bearing keys are stripped. `json_remove` is safe here since `annotate_event` already relies on SQLite JSON1. [events.rs:168-200](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_ed78398f_l6be7hp0/src/storage/events.rs)

**`src/storage/crud_batch.rs`** — wired the scrub into all three destruction paths:
- `tombstone_entity_with_timestamp` scrubs after the tombstone `UPDATE` succeeds (events keep `entity_id` — the tombstone preserves audit history, minus the text)
- `delete_entity_cascade` and `delete_entities_cascade_batch` scrub *before* `entity_id` is nullified — once NULL, the rows no longer match the entity [crud_batch.rs:144-147](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_ed78398f_l6be7hp0/src/storage/crud_batch.rs)
